name: base
_patch_note: patch 0 = full image. Measured receptive field is 72 px (16 blocks) / 104 px (24 blocks); a 64 px crop is smaller than that, so cropped training would feed the network zero-padding it never sees at inference.
_amp_note: amp:false is MEASURED, not an oversight. On this GTX 1650 (Turing TU117, no tensor cores) fp16 autocast is 5x SLOWER than fp32: 4.0 img/s vs 20.1 img/s. On a GPU with tensor cores (T4, A100, H100) re-benchmark -- amp:true will very likely win there.
_bench_note: fp32 sweep on GTX 1650, full 128x128 images: 64ch/16blk 20.1 img/s (2.34 GiB) | 64ch/24blk 14.0 | 96ch/16blk 10.0 | 96ch/24blk 7.1. channels_last was slower (15.6). Bigger models cost more epochs than the capacity is worth in one overnight run.
_epoch_note: 110 epochs = MEASURED 191 s/epoch (fp32, batch 12, incl. data loading and 200-image validation) x 110 = 5.8 h, sized to the overnight window so the cosine schedule anneals over exactly the run. A half-annealed cosine ships a worse model than a shorter schedule run to completion.
